football_evidence.question: Can North Carolina take away Syracuse’s big plays?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward North Carolina, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.0 of the 2.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Syracuse has the ball (the red zone): Syracuse’s offense succeeds on 33.6% of its red-zone plays, and North Carolina’s defense allows success on 32.6% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When Syracuse has the ball (big plays on the ground): Syracuse’s offense turns 4.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and North Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When North Carolina has the ball (the red zone): North Carolina’s offense succeeds on 38.6% of its red-zone plays, and Syracuse’s defense allows success on 58.8% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When Syracuse has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Syracuse’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.4% of its dropbacks, and North Carolina’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
contradicting: When North Carolina has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): North Carolina’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.3% of its dropbacks, and Syracuse’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When North Carolina has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): North Carolina’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 14.8% of its runs, and Syracuse’s defense stops 24.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Syracuse has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Syracuse’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 19.1% of its runs, and North Carolina’s defense stops 9.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Syracuse’s receivers No. 7 nationally and North Carolina’s No. 65.
quarterbacks: Billy Edwards Jr. has completed 94 of 158 passes (59.5%) for 1,259 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for North Carolina, and has been sacked on 13 of 171 dropbacks.
Steve Angeli has completed 58 of 104 passes (55.8%) for 720 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in three games for Syracuse, and has been sacked on 8 of 112 dropbacks.
Malachi Nelson has completed 42 of 70 passes (60.0%) for 532 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in three games for Syracuse, and has been sacked on 5 of 75 dropbacks.
